question.text: Deep cyclical industries like capital goods experience:

answer.text: Stable revenues regardless of economic conditions
Extreme cyclicality driven by economic and commodity cycles
Consistent dividend payments in all phases

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says deep cyclical industries witness extreme cyclicality in revenues driven by economic and/or commodity cycles. Capital goods and steel are named as examples, and sales drop significantly during recessions as customers defer capacity expansion. The Trap: "Stable revenues regardless of economic conditions" describes defensive industries (utilities, FMCG staples), not deep cyclicals. Deep cyclicals are highly sensitive to government policy on infrastructure spend and to commodity prices, not insulated from them. Note: Deep cyclicals are the opposite of defensives — their earnings and revenues swing materially with the economic and commodity cycle.
